unsupported_claims: The authors built the co-author network by taking the publication records in their dataset, treating each author as a node, and adding an edge between two authors whenever they had coauthored at least one paper.
After this filtering step, the final network contained 1,024 authors (nodes) and 3,842 co-author links (edges).
rationale: The evidence supports that the co-author network was built from papers published in six conferences across three fields, and that authors with degree less than 3 were filtered out. However, the answer invents an unsupported construction detail and gives incorrect final network size and edge count; the paper reports 18,561 authors and 207,074 edges.
